title: Hideo Kojima Reviews The Resident Evil Movie
summary:
Writer-director Hideo Kojima has seen Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, and he has now shared his review. Kojima, a true cinephile known for his public movie reviews, said he "wasn't particularly interested" in seeing the movie at first, but he did, and he sounded pretty impressed by what he saw.

"Right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of The Thing. From there, it’s a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end," he said.

Kojima went on to observe what others did as well, which is how the Resident Evil movie is more of a film that provides the "experience of playing Resident Evil" as opposed to watching an adaptation of one of its stories.

"It reminded me of how I felt when I first played the original Resident Evil on PlayStation back in 1996," he said. "I was just like [main character] Bryan in this movie. I kept getting game over after game over, shouting “F***!” over and over again. lol."

This is the kind of response that Cregger said he wanted viewers to have. It's also what got Cregger in some hot water with hardcore fans who wanted to see a straight adaptation of one of the games instead of Cregger's own original story set inside the world of Resident Evil.

Another bright spot for Kojima? While he was at the theater, he picked up some physical reading materials for the divisive new Tom Cruise movie Digger. A lot of people have had a lot of things to say about that film, and we are all waiting to hear what Kojima thought of it, whenever he sees it.

The new Resident Evil has made more than $320 million worldwide, following its big debut in China where it's made $40.7 million so far. Cregger's Resident Evil movie is now the highest-grossing entry in the series to date, surpassing the previous record-holder, which was 2016's The Final Chapter ($312 million).

For more, check out GameSpot's rundown of the highest-grossing Resident Evil movies of all time.

While Cregger has said he has ideas for another Resident Evil movie, he’s done with franchise movies and is instead making an original movie, The Flood, next.

As for Kojima, he's keeping very busy with the upcoming games OD and Phsyint, both of which are in the works for Xbox. Physint will also be adapted for film and TV, while Kojima's Death Stranding is coming to the big screen as well.

title: Here Are The Highest-Grossing Resident Evil Movies Ever, And The New One Is Now No. 1
summary:
Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie got solid reviews and is making a lot of money at the box office, but where does it rank on the list of highest-grossing Resident Evil movies? Following its debut in China, it's now No. 1 overall.

Director Paul W.S. Anderson made six previous Resident Evil movies, starring his wife, Milla Jovovich, and 2016's The Final Chapter previously ranked No. 1 in terms of money at the box office. Anderson's movies did not fare very well with critics, but had dedicated fans who kept going to see them. Together, Anderson's six movies made more than $1 billion.

Cregger's Resident Evil movie now ranks No. 1 with more than $320 million worldwide. It's also Cregger's highest-grossing movie ever, surpassing Weapons ($270 million).

Below you can see a rundown of the highest-grossing live-action Resident Evil movies ever, including domestic, international, and global figures. In addition to Cregger and Anderson, director Johannes Roberts worked on the series for 2021's Welcome to Raccoon City, the lowest-performing Resident Evil live-action movie ever.

The Resident Evil movies are produced by Constantin Films, which bought the rights back in the '90s and has retained them ever since. After Welcome to Raccoon City flopped, Constantin planned to put the film franchise on ice ... until Cregger showed up with a pitch.

While Cregger has said he has ideas for another Resident Evil movie, he's done with franchise movies and is instead making an original movie, The Flood, next.

title: Battlefield 6 Now Lets You Instantly Unlock All Guns At 100% Mastery For $30
summary:
It's a big week for Battlefield 6, as the game just launched its big Season 5 update, arrived on Xbox Game Pass, and ushered in a new Game of the Year Edition. That's not all, however, as the military shooter added a big new microtransaction in the form of the Ultimate Shortcut Kit.

Similar to how these shortcut kits worked in past Battlefield games, Battlefield 6's $30 no-so-microtransaction instantly unlocks all of the game's guns for all four classes, and at 100% Mastery--this means they are fully leveled up and kitted out.

People online have raised concerns about the existence of the Ultimate Shortcut Kit, saying it's unfair to allow people to buy every gun right from the start instead of grinding to progress. Other people said they welcome the Ultimate Shortcut Kit because they do not have the time or the interest in spending countless hours levelling up their guns and just want to play everything the game has to offer.

In addition to all the guns, the Ultimate Shortcut Kit for Battlefield 6 includes the Mortal Shriek dog tag and the Field Training: Cross Trained title. Below is a rundown of everything you get in the Ultimate Shortcut Kit.

Similar Ultimate Shortcut Kits for Battlefield 3 ($40) and Battlefield 4 ($50) cost more.

Battlefield 6 was 2025's best-selling game in the US, reportedly selling more than 20 million units in about three months. Despite the game's enormous success, EA cut staff at the studio after launch.

Battlefield 6 Ultimate Shortcut Kit:

Assault Shortcut Kit:

  • 7 Weapons (100% Mastery)
  • 2 Vehicles (100% Mastery)
  • Frontliner Training Path
  • 4 Gadgets

Support Shortcut Kit:

  • 7 Weapons (100% Mastery)
  • 2 Vehicles (100% Mastery)

  • 4 Gadgets

Engineer Shortcut Kit:

  • 7 Weapons (100% Mastery)
  • 2 Vehicles (100% Mastery)
  • Combat Engineer Training Path
  • 7 Gadgets

Recon Shortcut Kit:

  • 7 Weapons (100% Mastery)
  • 2 Vehicles (100% Mastery)
  • Spec Ops Training Path
  • 4 Gadgets

title: Despite Huge Changes For The Series, Halo Fest 2026 Is Going Forward, And News Is Coming Soon
summary:
The big Halo Fest event planned for December is going ahead as planned, despite mass layoffs and other major changes at developer Halo Studios.

Halo Studios director of competitive engagement, Tashi, confirmed this and said there will be news about Halo Fest this week. Additionally, Halo Studios will release materials "celebrating the community and 25 years of Halo," while fans can also look forward to "relevant game info" about in-market Halo games.

"There's a huge amount of Halo fans who are looking forward to the event to attend or watch from home, and we're looking forward to providing a platform for the community to celebrate 25 years of Halo and each other," Tashi said of Halo Fest.

Halo Fest takes place December 11-13 in Seattle--the event is totally sold out. "No matter why you love Halo, whether it’s the story and characters, the music, the art and universe, or just playing with friends--Halo Fest will have something for you," Microsoft said of the event.

The voices of Master Chief and Cortana, Steve Downes and Jen Taylor, will appear at Halo Fest, while there will also be a range of community events celebrating the series. Some had expected Halo Studios to announce the next big Halo game at Halo Fest, but it's not unreasonable to think that plans may have changed.

Halo Fest is happening against a major shift for the Halo franchise following the gutting of Halo Studios and the transition of the series from Halo Studios to Activision. Halo Studios now employs a significantly smaller team that will support already-released Halo games like Halo: The Master Chief Collection and Halo Infinite, but future games in the series--including the rumored reboot--will be made at Activision.

Halo Studios was rumored to be working on Halo 2 and Halo 3 remakes, as well as a new live-service Halo game. That was before the big changes, however, and it's been reported that Activision is working on a Halo reboot.

title: Red Dead’s Shocking Twist Ending Angered A Lot Of People, But It Was The Right Call, Rockstar Co-Founder Says
summary:
Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser has recalled the controversial ending to 2010's Red Dead Redemption in which the main character, John Marston, is killed.

He said in an interview that the game's lead designer, Christian Cantamessa was on board with the idea to kill off Marston, but Houser wondered about the production realities of, "How does an open-world game work if you've killed the protagonist?"

"So I said, ‘I think maybe we have to kill him.’ And he goes, ‘That's a great idea. Got to do it.’ I said, ‘I don't know if… let me just think about this,’ because we're just dealing with audio and dialogue," Houser told IGN "The nature of an open-world game is you finish a story, then you go back into the world and wrap up all the side content if you want to. We'd have to play as someone else for that. We could play as Jack, but what does that mean? So I had to think through for a while what it would mean production-wise.”

How Rockstar handled it was by setting RDR's epilogue years later, in the year 1914, with players taking control of Marston's son, Jack. He said this setup presented challenges, too, in terms of the technical realities of playing as Jack as opposed to John. There were story and mission concerns, too, including how multi-stage missions might play out if players, as John, completed one part and then came back to finish later as Jack.

"How would that work? We had to think through all of that stuff and concluded we could probably make it work, but we were still scared," he said.

The RDR epilogue has Jack hunting down and killing the men who killed his father, and Houser said players "really loved" that feeling of vengeance. Ultimately, Houser observed that there was "broad consensus" that it was the right call in the end to kill off John, even if it was an "unusual and out-there decision." Houser was, however, surprised by "how angry some people were about that decision."

"There were people who were livid with you. And part of you goes, ‘That's fantastic,’ because it means you've really engaged in the story and the characters," he said. "Now, I think it was the right decision because you want those big, strong reactions, but I think people were really confused by it. As a writer, it was like he had to die for the story to have any weight."

Also in the interview, Houser said he wanted to achieve something like this in the GTA franchise, but it never happened due to technical reasons.

He and the Rockstar team did, however, pull it off again with Red Dead Redemption II, which is a prequel to the earlier game. RDR2 famously killed off its own main playable character, Arthur Morgan, though he died from tuberculosis or at the hand of Micah. RDR 2 had an epilogue as well, featuring John and Jack Marston.

Houser left Rockstar in 2020 and now works at Absurd Ventures, which is crafting an open-world comedy game. His brother, Sam Houser, remains at Rockstar and helped lead the team bringing GTA 6 to market on November 19.

title: METRO 2039 – Official Pre-Order Gameplay Trailer
summary:
Pre-orders for METRO 2039 are now open, and we are revealing the editions that will be available on launch day, come February 4th 2027!

We know many of you can’t wait to get your hands on the next METRO, and are in desperate need of a wearable Spartan Helmet replica to add to your gaming collection. Well, the day has come to secure it!

We recently revealed that Blueprints are a new feature in METRO 2039, encouraging exploration and allowing you to craft upgrades and attachments for weapons and gear. The Specialist Pack pre-order bonus, available for all pre-ordered editions, gives you the opportunity to unlock these early. There are three upgrades to choose from, but you can only equip one at a time – choose wisely!

The Deluxe Edition also gives extra loot for the discerning stalker – both the immersive journey in music - the official game soundtrack and the gorgeous visuals of the concept art book are included, for both physical and digital editions. Not to mention access to the Story Expansion DLC to be released in 2027.

The Collector’s Edition, if you haven’t already seen it, is a great way to become a part of METRO history – featuring that wearable Spartan Helmet replica and the full contents of the Deluxe Edition and the pre-order bonus, it is the best way to become fully immersed in the world of METRO 2039. Display it as a prized art piece or wear it to your next cosplay event (or work zoom call).

title: Battlefield 6 Comes To Game Pass, Game Of The Year Edition Announced
summary:
It's a big day for Xbox Game Pass, as developer Battlefield Studios has launched Battlefield 6 into Game Pass, and it comes at a big moment for the game.

Battlefield 6 is now available for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate ($23/month) subscribers on PC and console. It can also be streamed.

The game's arrival in Game Pass is notable because Battlefield 6 was 2025's best-selling game overall in the US, and was released a year ago this month. The game had a very strong start, but player numbers have dropped. Battlefield Studios is attempting to reignite the fanbase in a number of ways, including bringing the game to Game Pass and continuing to support the FPS with big new updates. The latest of these, the Season 5 update, is out today, October 13.

Season 5 adds a new maps, including environments set in Las Vegas and Area 51, while it also brings something fans have been asking for since launch: a proper server browser. Check out the gameplay trailer above to see the Season 5 content in action.

Additionally, Battlefield Studios announced a Game of the Year Edition for Battlefield 6. The biggest selling point for the GOTY edition is the Ultimate Shortcut Kit, which instantly unlocks everything for all four classes, along with one season of Battlefield Pro, among other digital perks and extras.

The Ultimate Shortcut Kit, which was also available in other previous Battlefield games, is available to purchase by itself for $30.

title: God Of War’s Laufey Collector’s Edition Leaves One Important Thing Out: The Game
summary:
The God of War Laufey Collector's Edition has been revealed, but unlike the standard and digital deluxe editions that went up for preorder last month, this is purely a box of merch. The main attraction of this collector's edition is an eight-inch statue of Faye, Phranque the Cube, and Rue fighting against Begtse’s soldiers. Phranque will light up when connected to a USB power source.

The set also includes a deck of 51 illustrated oracle cards and a mini art book depicting the characters, creatures, and environments of God of War Laufey, all housed in collector's edition-packaging. As noted in the image, God of War Laufey is sold separately, and this edition costs $150. You'll need to shell out another $70 for a physical edition of the game to complete it. Preorders are now live on the PlayStation Direct Store ahead of the game's February 2027 release.

Sony has released several collector's editions in the past that bundled a digital download key for a game. A merchandise-only box set isn't uncommon, as just a few weeks ago, Rockstar Games revealed the $400 GTA 6 collector's edition that comes with plenty of stuff.

So what's the thinking behind one of these boxes? These boxes typically target dedicated, high-spending superfans who can afford to shell out extra for bonus physical content like this, acting as high-margin merchandise. At the same time, publishers can save some cash by not including the game, streamlining their supply chains and lowering production overhead in the process. Essentially, a bigger slice of the pie for companies, while consumers with deep pockets get limited-edition swag to display.

In other God of War news, the next game in the series will see Kratos return to the spotlight, and it'll pick up directly after the end of God of War Laufey. A live-action God of War TV series is also in development for Prime Video, and its new leading man, Dave Bautista, is already working to get shredded for the role after the original Kratos actor, Ryan Hurst, departed due to injury.

title: Best Witcher 3 Mods To Download For The Remaster
summary:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is considered one of the best RPGs of all time, but community members have still managed to design some incredible mods that alter, expand on, and improve it. Even after the Remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released, mod creators still managed to enhance the experience in one way or another.

Mods for The Witcher 3 range from quality-of-life changes, to redesigns of gameplay mechanics, to full-on DLC add-ons with new quests and content. While The Witcher 3 doesn’t have quite the expansive library of mods that Skyrim or Fallout 4 do on Nexus Mods, there are still dozens that make the game better in one way or another.

Below, you can see our picks for the 28 best mods to download for The Witcher 3. The mods are listed in no particular order, and all of these have been confirmed to be compatible with the Remastered version of the game. Also of note: cross-platform mod support for The Witcher 3 is fully functional in the Remastered version, but not every mod will necessarily be supported on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Better Call Ciri

  • Created by: pMarK
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Ciri sections in The Witcher 3 are some of the best parts of the entire game, as the young Witcher has so many unique abilities that Geralt simply doesn't have. Unfortunately, Ciri's sections are few and far between in the base game, but you can change that with the click of a button using the Better Call Siri mod.

This mod allows you to instantly change between Geralt and Ciri, regardless of where you are in The Witcher 3. You'll also have access to all of Ciri's abilities, and she can even fast travel and use Roach. However, you won't be able to earn XP as Ciri.

Advertisement

Monsters Reworked

  • Created by: Denroth
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The creatures of The Witcher 3 get their due in Monsters Reworked, an expansive mod that tackles all of the monsters in the game and its expansion. Denroth enhanced the visuals and modified more than textures to bring this project to fruition, and it’s truly an evolutionary step forward for the game.

In some cases, a complete or partial rework of the monsters was necessary to bring them up to a modern-gen standard. Those creatures have never looked better than they did after this. If anything, it makes battling the monsters even more fun, but be careful you don't get distracted admiring them while you’re trying to fight a battle. That’s just going to lead Geralt to a fatal end.

Advertisement

Tales of The Witcher

  • Created by: Gerwant
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

How’s this for ambition? Gerwant’s Tales of the Witcher jettisons the story of both the game and The Witcher novels, replacing them with a tale that takes place during Geralt’s first adventure in Cintra. It’s a brand-new story, with an emphasis on exploration and killing monsters. It feels like the expansion we never got, even though Tales of the Witcher remains a work in progress.

This mod was created with REDkit, and Gerwant has kept new updates coming since its release. For the final version, Gerwant is shooting for 25 hours of gameplay, 20 main quests, and a map that’s twice the size of The Witcher 3’s prologue playground map.

Custom Player Character

  • Created by: nikich340
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

This is one of the most intriguing Witcher 3 mods, because it gives players the chance to create their own characters and insert them into the game’s storyline. It not only offers fans the chance to set their character’s gender, it also has distinct male and female voices to choose from.

You could make your character a Witcher, but the more exciting aspect of this mod is that you can also choose to be a Sorceress. That entails a completely new combat system for magical attacks and a unique quest. Picking this option is like paving the way for a spin-off you never knew you wanted.

Advertisement

Firearms

  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Witcher 3 doesn’t have firearms, but this mod solves that problem by giving Geralt access to several weapons. Essentially, it allows Geralt to shoot his enemies in addition to all of his other attacks. Mod creator Roenaxx also added some thoughtful touches to keep this addition from unbalancing the game. The guns aren’t for sale, and players will have to complete a progression path to open them. Even if you do see that quest through to the end, bullets are going to be scarce.

If you want to stay well-armed in this world, then you’re gonna have to work for it by tracking down the materials you’ll need to craft bullets. You'll also need the Firearms compatibility mod to have it work with the Remastered version of The Witcher 3.

Advertisement

All Quest Objectives On Map

  • Created by: Wolfmark
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Witcher 3 is a game chock-full of quests you can take on. By default, you can only track one of these quests on the map at a time, which can get slightly tedious if you have multiple objectives in one location. If you download the All Quest Objectives On Map mod, though, you'll be able to track all of your quests at the same time and view them on the map, so you know exactly where to go for each of them.

Advertisement

Over 9000

  • Download link: Nexus Mods

When you're out adventuring in the world, slaying monsters, and looting enemies, your inventory will get quite full, quite fast. You'll often find yourself dropping some valuable loot that you would have liked to carry, if only Geralt's pockets could handle it. To solve that issue, the Over 9000 mod makes it so you'll hopefully never exceed your carrying capacity again. The mod makes your carrying weight 9,000 pounds, which you'll likely never get near unless you're picking up every junk item you can find.

Advertisement

Fast Travel from Anywhere

  • Created by: JupiterTheGod
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

One of the more frustrating aspects of The Witcher 3 is being forced to make your way to signposts in order to fast travel to a destination. If you're not a fan of that mechanic, you can download the Fast Travel from Anywhere mod, which does exactly what the title says. No longer do you have to be at a signpost to fast travel; you can instead open your map and fast travel to any signpost you've previously visited on the map.

Advertisement

Sprint in Witcher Senses

  • Created by: MerseyRockoff
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

You might not realize it during your playthrough, but you spend quite a bit of time in Witcher Senses mode in The Witcher 3. The mechanic is used during dozens of quests, and it's required to progress in the game. However, Witcher Senses stops your ability to sprint, which can make the mechanic feel very sluggish to use.

To speed up your time while in the mode, though, all you have to do is download the Sprint in Witcher Senses mod. Now, you can move freely while using Witcher Senses and save quite a bit of time when tracking a beast or following a human's footsteps or blood trail.

Advertisement

Friendly HUD

  • Created by: wghost81
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The default heads-up display in The Witcher 3 is perfectly adequate, but if you're playing for a second or eighth time, you might want to change things up. The Friendly HUD mod makes a slew of changes to the vanilla HUD and even lets you customize what's shown on it. The mod also adds 3D quest and map markers, providing you with a more in-depth look at what an area holds. You're able to add and remove elements from the HUD while in-game using the mod's commands.

Advertisement

Switchable Cloaks

  • Created by: Priler
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

If you've read The Witcher books or watched the Netflix TV show, you know Geralt of Rivia is rarely seen without his famous cloak. In The Witcher 3, though, Geralt doesn't wear a cloak, instead opting for a set of brown armor by default. With the Geralt Cloak mod, you can fix that and make Geralt look like he does in the show and the books. The cloak is made of a dark fabric and covers Geralt's head, but it also comes with a cape. You can equip and take off both the cape and the hood through the mod's commands, as well as choose where and when the cloak and cape are shown.

Advertisement

The Gwent Card Dealer

  • Created by: Mangekyoumadara1987
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Gwent is one of the most popular aspects of The Witcher 3, and it has even inspired a full video game of its own that has become one of the best titles on Steam. However, trying to play Gwent properly in The Witcher 3 can be a slight hassle, as you have to collect more and more powerful cards as you progress. This becomes an issue, as Gwent cards are extremely hard to find. Of course, if you download The Gwent Card Dealer mod, you can bypass the grind of finding the cards yourself. This new merchant in The Witcher 3 sells 99% of cards, with some exceptions being those unique cards that you can only acquire in one specific way.

Advertisement

More Money For Traders

  • Created by: Tommy1984
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Traders in The Witcher 3 are an extremely useful resource, as they sell gear and items you need, as well as take unneeded loot off your hands for some quick cash. Unfortunately, the traders around the map often don't carry much money, leaving you to visit multiple traders to sell off all of your junk. With the More Money For Traders mod, though, that no longer becomes a problem. All traders on the map now restock their money supply every time you visit them, and have more cash to spend in general.

Advertisement

Slots Slots Slots

  • Created by: Krdemolition4
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

If you want to become truly overpowered in The Witcher 3, then you want as many skill sockets and mutation slots as possible. By default, you don’t have a ton of either, but the Slots Slots Slots mod changes that. The mod bumps the skill sockets from 12 and 16 to 18 and 26, while also adding four new mutation slots. You can now make Geralt a much tougher Witcher and utilize a more in-depth build.

Advertisement

Gallop Anywhere No Panic

  • Created by: alx713
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

When you arrive inside a major city in The Witcher 3, you immediately have some movement restrictions. Specifically, if you're riding Roach, you can only ride at a very slow pace through the city streets. Thanks to the Galloping In Cities mod, though, that restriction is fully lifted, allowing you to gallop through cities regardless of where you are, and making traveling to your destination a much quicker affair.

Advertisement

No Level Requirements

  • Created by: Dominitk666
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Every Witcher 3 player has experienced the sullen feeling of looting a new piece of gear and realizing they're not at the right level to equip it. You never have to experience that feeling again after downloading the No Level Requirements mod, as this makes it so every item and gear piece can be equipped regardless of your current level.

Advertisement

God Mode

  • Created by: jgheld and tnovak
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

God Mode is a mod that allows you to turn The Witcher 3 into whatever kind of game you want. The mod allows you to customize everything about your experience, turning the RPG into your personal playground. At the center of God Mode is the ability to become invincible, as you can reduce all enemy damage to zero so that Geralt never loses any HP. However, the mod can also give you unlimited money, items, carrying capacity, and a slew of other benefits that make The Witcher 3 easier. It's only recommended to download this mod if you're struggling with the game's mechanics and enemies, or if you've played through more than once.

Advertisement

Critical Slow Motion Combat Mod

  • Created by: KNGR, ksolberg, Halfmillz
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Combat in The Witcher 3 isn't everyone's cup of tea, and if you've been looking for a way to spice up your encounters with enemies, consider the Critical Slow Motion Combat mod. It adds a new slow motion element to combat, giving you the chance to outmaneuver enemies in a pinch and deal more damage in the process. There are new animations added with the mod, and you can choose when to activate the slow-mo while in combat.

Advertisement

Gwent Redux

  • Created by: oerdi25
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Gwent is a mini-game that can stretch over hours in The Witcher 3. However, if you're looking to get even more out of the card game, you can download the Gwent Redux mod. It makes changes to the default cards, adds more than 100 new cards to your potential deck, improves opponent AI, and alters other parts of Gwent to make it more balanced and enjoyable. The mod changes quite a bit, so make sure you read its description to see everything that comes with downloading it.

Advertisement

Unlimited Roach Stamina

  • Created by: liongvn
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

We all love Roach as a character, but as a horse, he can be quite annoying at times. One of the more frustrating things about Roach is how quickly his stamina depletes, forcing you to slowly meander a path until the stamina recharges. Luckily, the Infinite Roach Stamina mod allows Roach to never stop galloping in The Witcher 3. With the mod installed, Roach never has to recharge his stamina bar, which is quite useful for the horse races on the map or in general travel.

Advertisement

Witcher 3 Quests Extended

  • Created by: PaulR0013
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The quests in The Witcher 3 are some of the deepest and most enjoyable you'll find in an RPG. However, after you've done them all multiple times, they can get a little stale. If you're searching for new quests to take on, grab the Witcher 3 Quests Extended mod. It adds 18 new quests to the game, some of which require either the Hearts of Stone or Blood and Wine expansions. However, there are plenty of quests that can be accessed in the base game, too. Check out the mod's description page to see how and where to start these quests.

Advertisement

Immersive Sounds

  • Created by: TheMenxceX
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Witcher 3's gameplay sounds are iconic. However, the Immersive Sounds mod takes the sounds you hear while exploring and in combat to another level. The mod makes all of the sounds clearer and punchier, adding some impact behind your in-game actions.

Advertisement

Yet Another Crossbow Rework

  • Created by: blibby84
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The crossbow isn't the strongest weapon in the default version of The Witcher 3. While it can be used to kill some lower-level enemies or enemies who are tough to reach, you're rarely clamoring to pull the crossbow out in a tense situation. That thought process can be changed with the Crossbow Rework mod, though, which makes the crossbow much stronger in general by balancing all of its in-game stats. Moreover, as you upgrade your crossbow, it becomes significantly stronger than the last one you had equipped.

Advertisement

Witcher 2 Potion Length

  • Created by: mindkiller316
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Potions are crucial to your survival in The Witcher 3, especially if you're playing on one of the harder difficulty levels. The potions you use tend not to last very long, though, which can lead you to constantly going to acquire more ingredients for your concoctions. The Witcher 2 Potion Length mod fixes that dilemma by making every potion you consume last much longer. This reverts the potion duration back to what it was in The Witcher 2, which allows you to feel the effects of potions for several minutes.

Advertisement

Blood And Steel

  • Created by: Riyusso
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Blood and Steel mod for The Witcher 3 changes up combat in several different ways. The mod aims to make targeting and dodging more intuitive, while also adding new and improved animations to all elements of combat. The most noticeable change the mod makes is to the dodging mechanic, which is now much faster and more reactive, allowing you to escape a sticky situation with more precision. You'll also see changes to the combat camera and sign usage, and to the fighting styles of enemies.

Advertisement

Increased Creature Loot

  • Created by: mindkiller316
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

There's nothing worse in The Witcher 3 than defeating a creature, big or small, and opening up their inventory to find almost nothing of value. While you might loot a small trinket or resource that you can sell, you often want to see more lootable items after you've slain a monster. The Increased Creature Loot mod comes equipped with that sole goal, making it so every single creature in The Witcher 3 drops some sort of loot and ups the quantity you'll find after killing something.

Advertisement

No Time For Gwent

  • Created by: Fluffy82
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

To most The Witcher 3 players, Gwent is one of the best parts of the entire game. It's become a game by itself, and you can easily spend over a dozen hours playing it in The Witcher 3. However, whether you don't like Gwent or you don't have time for it at a certain point during your playthrough, you can download the No Time For Gwent mod, which allows you to use Axii to immediately win your current game. After using the sign, you'll proceed to the dialogue between Geralt and the other NPC and move on with your journey.

title: Xbox Is Testing A New Streak Feature That Could Make Gaming Feel (More) Like A Chore
summary:
It looks like another new Xbox feature is in development, and this time, it's designed to encourage users to go on a hot streak--of using their console, not disrupting a sports event with a quick birthday-suit-run.

Spotted by Game File's Stephen Totilo, a new number appears to be popping up on the dashboard of Xbox users who are signed up for the Xbox Insider program, suggesting that a streak counter is in development. Microsoft hasn't formally announced this feature yet, and it looks like it kicks in after using your Xbox for three days in a row per week. It's an idea that Microsoft has experimented with in the past through Game Pass and the Xbox mobile app, but never to this extent with a prominent display of how many days in a row you've dedicated to playing Xbox games.

Is there any benefit to Streaks for Xbox users? Totilo's research suggests that it could be tied to Xbox reward points, which can be redeemed for digital items and Xbox gift cards. On Microsoft's side, this could also be a subtle way to keep users engaged more consistently, since the lure of a score streak is powerful. Just look at Wordle, with its subtle emphasis on keeping your streak going, or mobile free-to-play games that offer daily login rewards to tempt you to sign in regularly.

That could be good, bad, or irritating depending on how it is implemented, as Xbox users could find themselves regularly pinged on their progress while they're in the middle of a game. Your tolerance mileage might vary when it comes to these notifications, so hopefully there's an opt-out option if Streaks roll out. But as Totilo noted, just because Xbox is testing this new streak function doesn't mean it'll be implemented across the Xbox ecosystem in the future. The fine print for Xbox Insiders mentions that these features may not become "permanent additions" to Xbox.

One new addition to Xbox that has been confirmed are Mythic Achievements, which are designed to be proof of your accomplishments in a given video game. Similar to PlayStation Platinum Trophies, a Mythic Achievement is earned whenever all of the original achievements for a game have been earned.

title: GTA 6 Will Reportedly Come To PC Much Earlier Than Expected
summary:
The November launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will leave PC gamers sitting out in the cold, but the wait for the yet-to-be-announced PC port might be surprisingly short this time. According to a new report, GTA 6 will launch on PC "within the first three months" of 2027.

Speaking to GamesBeat, industry sources claim that Rockstar Games plans to launch the game just a few months after its console release. If the reports are accurate, this would mark a major departure for Rockstar Games, as previous PC ports arrived long after their original console releases. GTA 5, for example, landed on PC 18 months after its PS3 and Xbox 360 release, while the PC version of Red Dead Redemption 2 appeared 11 months after its PS4 and Xbox One release.

Take-Two Interactive boss Strauss Zelnick previously commented that PC was becoming an important platform for the GTA 6 parent company to focus on, saying sales of the publisher's PC games had increased dramatically over the years. 

As for why GTA 6 won't be available on PC at launch, former Rockstar producer John Ricchio theorized that a console-first approach to development would give Rockstar more room to build a PC version later. Since consoles have limited hardware, it's easier for a studio to expand a game to run on more powerful hardware like a PC instead of scaling back to fit console constraints.

Rockstar hasn’t officially said anything about GTA 6 on PC yet, and the game officially lists only PS5 and Xbox Series X|S as its platforms. Xbox also recently clarified that GTA 6 will not be streamed to PC through Xbox Cloud Gaming, despite initial reports that Microsoft had secured exclusive streaming rights.

title: Fortnite Dev Reportedly Delays New Marvel/Star Wars Shooter Amid “AI Acceleration” Push
summary:
Unreal Engine and Fortnite maker Epic Games reportedly delayed an unannounced shooter featuring Marvel and Star Wars characters, and it's said that Epic is pushing its developers to utilize AI tools like Claude to complete production on the game.

Per Bloomberg, the collaboration with Disney was originally slated for a March 2027 release and is now without a date. According to Bloomberg, developers were directed to incorporate an "AI first" production model. An internal memo obtained by the outlet included the instruction: "No more hand-written code," adding that artwork would be "generated with full AI workflows."

Epic Games did not address the purported existence of this Disney-themed shooter, but Epic's communications director Jake Jones provided a statement to Bloomberg, saying: "We’re embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do."

Shortly before Bloomberg's report went live, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney posted on social media about the company's "huge pivot" toward "maximum AI acceleration" for game development--a move Sweeney believes would benefit "all teams using Unreal."

Sweeney elaborated in subsequent posts, adding that Epic's "modest aim" is to "survive the AI revolution, help other developers do the same, and come out on the other end making better code and content faster."

That pivot to an AI-focused model appears to be a key component of Epic 's collaboration with Disney. AI consultant and "Metaverse artist" Lachlan Phillips, who directed four Disney experiences for Fortnite, stated on social media that he advocated for "AI-heavy workflow across coding and art."

Disney has heavily invested in Epic Games and Fortnite ($1.5 billion, to be exact), and the two companies are working on multiple gaming projects together. A report earlier in 2026 claimed that one of these projects was an extraction shooter starring Disney characters, though it is unclear if this is the same project as the Marvel/Star Wars shooter Bloomberg has reported on.

Regardless, gaming appears to be a key priority for Disney under CEO Josh D'Amaro, who began his tenure in the top executive position earlier in 2026.

“Interactive platforms are an increasingly relevant medium for younger audiences to engage with characters and stories, and our collaboration with Epic Games is central to our efforts in this space,” D'Amaro said in May. “Our characters are among the most popular across the Fortnite universe.”

Despite rumors that Disney is looking to acquire Epic Games, Disney executive Dana Walden said that such talks were "not the conversations we’re having right now," adding that Disney and Epic have "a great partnership.”

title: Every GameSpot 10/10 Review Score
summary:
The gaming essentials.

It isn't often that we give 10/10 review scores on GameSpot. Since the site was founded in 1996, only 30 games have earned that rank. But to achieve a 10/10, a game needs to be essential, and it needs to have something so meaningful to offer us that it simply cannot be ignored. Regardless, a 10/10 review score is always determined by the personal opinion of its respective writer and always reflects as such. So without further ado, here is a list of all the games that we've scored with a 10/10! For more details on the review process and what a 10/10 means at GameSpot, check out our in-depth Q&A below.

What makes a game a 10, and has that definition changed over the years? Does a 10 mean it's "perfect"?

A 10 does not mean a game is perfect, but it does mean that it's a game we believe everyone should play. In our opinion, no game can be considered perfect. That means you may see a game getting a 10 despite having issues. It also means that games without obvious flaws may be scored below 10.

On the rare occasion when we publish a 10 review, that is our way of saying that no matter your preference for genre, developer, setting, or console, you owe it to yourself to find a way to play the game in question.

A review is obviously just one person's opinion, so how do you deal with conflicting thoughts on a game, both for high and low scores? What if someone else on GameSpot thinks a game deserves a much higher (or lower) score?

It's true that every review is an individual's take on a game, and sure enough, the many individuals within GameSpot often have differing opinions on the same game. This is something we accept, and we welcome diversity of opinion at the end of the day.

GameSpot's editorial team peer-reviews each other's work during the review process. This is not to determine whether we all agree on a score, but it allows us to ensure that the text we publish backs up the score that's issued. That means that there are reviews published where we may not all agree with the editor's opinion, but are otherwise confident enough in their argumentation to put our stamp on the review.

When the time comes that a score fails to align with the text as submitted, we will work together with the author to determine if they were able to effectively convey their thoughts relative to the score, and vice versa. We always encourage our writers to put their words down first and determine the score after the fact.

event_model_payload.headline: Every GameSpot 10/10 Review Score
event_model_payload.summary:
The gaming essentials.

It isn't often that we give 10/10 review scores on GameSpot. Since the site was founded in 1996, only 30 games have earned that rank. But to achieve a 10/10, a game needs to be essential, and it needs to have something so meaningful to offer us that it simply cannot be ignored. Regardless, a 10/10 review score is always determined by the personal opinion of its respective writer and always reflects as such. So without further ado, here is a list of all the games that we've scored with a 10/10! For more details on the review process and what a 10/10 means at GameSpot, check out our in-depth Q&A below.

What makes a game a 10, and has that definition changed over the years? Does a 10 mean it's "perfect"?

A 10 does not mean a game is perfect, but it does mean that it's a game we believe everyone should play. In our opinion, no game can be considered perfect. That means you may see a game getting a 10 despite having issues. It also means that games without obvious flaws may be scored below 10.

On the rare occasion when we publish a 10 review, that is our way of saying that no matter your preference for genre, developer, setting, or console, you owe it to yourself to find a way to play the game in question.

A review is obviously just one person's opinion, so how do you deal with conflicting thoughts on a game, both for high and low scores? What if someone else on GameSpot thinks a game deserves a much higher (or lower) score?

It's true that every review is an individual's take on a game, and sure enough, the many individuals within GameSpot often have differing opinions on the same game. This is something we accept, and we welcome diversity of opinion at the end of the day.

GameSpot's editorial team peer-reviews each other's work during the review process. This is not to determine whether we all agree on a score, but it allows us to ensure that the text we publish backs up the score that's issued. That means that there are reviews published where we may not all agree with the editor's opinion, but are otherwise confident enough in their argumentation to put our stamp on the review.

When the time comes that a score fails to align with the text as submitted, we will work together with the author to determine if they were able to effectively convey their thoughts relative to the score, and vice versa. We always encourage our writers to put their words down first and determine the score after the fact.

title: GTA 6 Fans Are Excited For Another Date In November, And It’s Not Release Day
summary:
Take-Two has announced the details for its next earnings briefing, and as you might expect, GTA 6 fans are circling the date on their calendars.

The next Take-Two quarterly earnings report will be released on Monday, November 9, with management holding a call at 1:30 PM PT / 4:30 PM ET that day to discuss the results and answer questions. Anyone can listen to the call online.

The report is being released 10 days before GTA 6 launches on November 19, so it's expected that analysts and investors will ask questions about the upcoming launch. Management, including CEO Strauss Zelnick, will likely have some kind of update or commentary to share.

However, fans should not hold out hope for any big details about the game itself, as those kinds of details historically come by way of developer Rockstar Games.

The next Take-Two earnings report is expected in February 2027, but if GTA 6 is the enormous success that everyone expects it to be, the company will likely share details about the game's commercial impact before then.

For GTA 5, Take-Two announced sales right away, confirming $800 million in revenue after the first 24 hours and $1 billion in revenue after three days.

If Sensor Tower's data is accurate, GTA 6 has already sold more than 6 million copies via pre-purchases, bringing in close to $600 million in revenue. Sensor Tower said the game could reach 25 million preorders by release, meaning the game will have made more than $2 billion before launch.

Take-Two investors are understandably excited about GTA 6's release, but the game stands to make even more money once the next evolution of GTA Online launches. To be sure, Rockstar has not yet announced any details about GTA 6's online component, and GTA 6 has been described as a single-player experience.

That being said, given the gigantic success of GTA Online in terms of popularity among fans and its moneymaking ability, it's a safe bet that Rockstar will bring online functionality to GTA 6 at some point.

Beyond any possible updates about GTA 6, the Take-Two earnings report and following call is expected to include updates on the company's numerous other franchises and studios. After all, the GTA franchise represents a very small part of Take-Two's overall business, accounting for less than 15% of total revenue. That number is for a typical quarter–when GTA 6 launches, it will significantly increase.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: Hideo Kojima Reviews The Resident Evil Movie
summary:
Writer-director Hideo Kojima has seen Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, and he has now shared his review. Kojima, a true cinephile known for his public movie reviews, said he "wasn't particularly interested" in seeing the movie at first, but he did, and he sounded pretty impressed by what he saw.

"Right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of The Thing. From there, it’s a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end," he said.

Kojima went on to observe what others did as well, which is how the Resident Evil movie is more of a film that provides the "experience of playing Resident Evil" as opposed to watching an adaptation of one of its stories.

"It reminded me of how I felt when I first played the original Resident Evil on PlayStation back in 1996," he said. "I was just like [main character] Bryan in this movie. I kept getting game over after game over, shouting “F***!” over and over again. lol."

This is the kind of response that Cregger said he wanted viewers to have. It's also what got Cregger in some hot water with hardcore fans who wanted to see a straight adaptation of one of the games instead of Cregger's own original story set inside the world of Resident Evil.

Another bright spot for Kojima? While he was at the theater, he picked up some physical reading materials for the divisive new Tom Cruise movie Digger. A lot of people have had a lot of things to say about that film, and we are all waiting to hear what Kojima thought of it, whenever he sees it.

The new Resident Evil has made more than $320 million worldwide, following its big debut in China where it's made $40.7 million so far. Cregger's Resident Evil movie is now the highest-grossing entry in the series to date, surpassing the previous record-holder, which was 2016's The Final Chapter ($312 million).

For more, check out GameSpot's rundown of the highest-grossing Resident Evil movies of all time.

While Cregger has said he has ideas for another Resident Evil movie, he’s done with franchise movies and is instead making an original movie, The Flood, next.

As for Kojima, he's keeping very busy with the upcoming games OD and Phsyint, both of which are in the works for Xbox. Physint will also be adapted for film and TV, while Kojima's Death Stranding is coming to the big screen as well.

title: Battlefield 6 Now Lets You Instantly Unlock All Guns At 100% Mastery For $30
summary:
It's a big week for Battlefield 6, as the game just launched its big Season 5 update, arrived on Xbox Game Pass, and ushered in a new Game of the Year Edition. That's not all, however, as the military shooter added a big new microtransaction in the form of the Ultimate Shortcut Kit.

Similar to how these shortcut kits worked in past Battlefield games, Battlefield 6's $30 no-so-microtransaction instantly unlocks all of the game's guns for all four classes, and at 100% Mastery--this means they are fully leveled up and kitted out.

People online have raised concerns about the existence of the Ultimate Shortcut Kit, saying it's unfair to allow people to buy every gun right from the start instead of grinding to progress. Other people said they welcome the Ultimate Shortcut Kit because they do not have the time or the interest in spending countless hours levelling up their guns and just want to play everything the game has to offer.

In addition to all the guns, the Ultimate Shortcut Kit for Battlefield 6 includes the Mortal Shriek dog tag and the Field Training: Cross Trained title. Below is a rundown of everything you get in the Ultimate Shortcut Kit.

Similar Ultimate Shortcut Kits for Battlefield 3 ($40) and Battlefield 4 ($50) cost more.

title: Despite Huge Changes For The Series, Halo Fest 2026 Is Going Forward, And News Is Coming Soon
summary:
The big Halo Fest event planned for December is going ahead as planned, despite mass layoffs and other major changes at developer Halo Studios.

Halo Studios director of competitive engagement, Tashi, confirmed this and said there will be news about Halo Fest this week. Additionally, Halo Studios will release materials "celebrating the community and 25 years of Halo," while fans can also look forward to "relevant game info" about in-market Halo games.

"There's a huge amount of Halo fans who are looking forward to the event to attend or watch from home, and we're looking forward to providing a platform for the community to celebrate 25 years of Halo and each other," Tashi said of Halo Fest.

Halo Fest takes place December 11-13 in Seattle--the event is totally sold out. "No matter why you love Halo, whether it’s the story and characters, the music, the art and universe, or just playing with friends--Halo Fest will have something for you," Microsoft said of the event.

The voices of Master Chief and Cortana, Steve Downes and Jen Taylor, will appear at Halo Fest, while there will also be a range of community events celebrating the series. Some had expected Halo Studios to announce the next big Halo game at Halo Fest, but it's not unreasonable to think that plans may have changed.

Halo Fest is happening against a major shift for the Halo franchise following the gutting of Halo Studios and the transition of the series from Halo Studios to Activision. Halo Studios now employs a significantly smaller team that will support already-released Halo games like Halo: The Master Chief Collection and Halo Infinite, but future games in the series--including the rumored reboot--will be made at Activision.

Halo Studios was rumored to be working on Halo 2 and Halo 3 remakes, as well as a new live-service Halo game. That was before the big changes, however, and it's been reported that Activision is working on a Halo reboot.

title: Red Dead’s Shocking Twist Ending Angered A Lot Of People, But It Was The Right Call, Rockstar Co-Founder Says
summary:
Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser has recalled the controversial ending to 2010's Red Dead Redemption in which the main character, John Marston, is killed.

He said in an interview that the game's lead designer, Christian Cantamessa was on board with the idea to kill off Marston, but Houser wondered about the production realities of, "How does an open-world game work if you've killed the protagonist?"

"So I said, ‘I think maybe we have to kill him.’ And he goes, ‘That's a great idea. Got to do it.’ I said, ‘I don't know if… let me just think about this,’ because we're just dealing with audio and dialogue," Houser told IGN "The nature of an open-world game is you finish a story, then you go back into the world and wrap up all the side content if you want to. We'd have to play as someone else for that. We could play as Jack, but what does that mean? So I had to think through for a while what it would mean production-wise.”

How Rockstar handled it was by setting RDR's epilogue years later, in the year 1914, with players taking control of Marston's son, Jack. He said this setup presented challenges, too, in terms of the technical realities of playing as Jack as opposed to John. There were story and mission concerns, too, including how multi-stage missions might play out if players, as John, completed one part and then came back to finish later as Jack.

"How would that work? We had to think through all of that stuff and concluded we could probably make it work, but we were still scared," he said.

The RDR epilogue has Jack hunting down and killing the men who killed his father, and Houser said players "really loved" that feeling of vengeance. Ultimately, Houser observed that there was "broad consensus" that it was the right call in the end to kill off John, even if it was an "unusual and out-there decision." Houser was, however, surprised by "how angry some people were about that decision."

"There were people who were livid with you. And part of you goes, ‘That's fantastic,’ because it means you've really engaged in the story and the characters," he said. "Now, I think it was the right decision because you want those big, strong reactions, but I think people were really confused by it. As a writer, it was like he had to die for the story to have any weight."

Also in the interview, Houser said he wanted to achieve something like this in the GTA franchise, but it never happened due to technical reasons.

He and the Rockstar team did, however, pull it off again with Red Dead Redemption II, which is a prequel to the earlier game. RDR2 famously killed off its own main playable character, Arthur Morgan, though he died from tuberculosis or at the hand of Micah. RDR 2 had an epilogue as well, featuring John and Jack Marston.

Houser left Rockstar in 2020 and now works at Absurd Ventures, which is crafting an open-world comedy game. His brother, Sam Houser, remains at Rockstar and helped lead the team bringing GTA 6 to market on November 19.

He said this setup presented challenges, too, in terms of the technical realities of playing as Jack as opposed to John. There were story and mission concerns, too, including how multi-stage missions might play out if players, as John, completed one part and then came back to finish later as Jack.

"How would that work? We had to think through all of that stuff and concluded we could probably make it work, but we were still scared," he said.

The RDR epilogue has Jack hunting down and killing the men who killed his father, and Houser said players "really loved" that feeling of vengeance. Ultimately, Houser observed that there was "broad consensus" that it was the right call in the end to kill off John, even if it was an "unusual and out-there decision." Houser was, however, surprised by "how angry some people were about that decision."

"There were people who were livid with you. And part of you goes, ‘That's fantastic,’ because it means you've really engaged in the story and the characters," he said. "Now, I think it was the right decision because you want those big, strong reactions, but I think people were really confused by it. As a writer, it was like he had to die for the story to have any weight."

Also in the interview, Houser said he wanted to achieve something like this in the GTA franchise, but it never happened due to technical reasons.

He and the Rockstar team did, however, pull it off again with Red Dead Redemption II, which is a prequel to the earlier game. RDR2 famously killed off its own main playable character, Arthur Morgan, though he died from tuberculosis or at the hand of Micah. RDR 2 had an epilogue as well, featuring John and Jack Marston.

Houser left Rockstar in 2020 and now works at Absurd Ventures, which is crafting an open-world comedy game. His brother, Sam Houser, remains at Rockstar and helped lead the team bringing GTA 6 to market on November 19.

title: Battlefield 6 Comes To Game Pass, Game Of The Year Edition Announced
summary:
It's a big day for Xbox Game Pass, as developer Battlefield Studios has launched Battlefield 6 into Game Pass, and it comes at a big moment for the game.

Battlefield 6 is now available for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate ($23/month) subscribers on PC and console. It can also be streamed.

The game's arrival in Game Pass is notable because Battlefield 6 was 2025's best-selling game overall in the US, and was released a year ago this month. The game had a very strong start, but player numbers have dropped. Battlefield Studios is attempting to reignite the fanbase in a number of ways, including bringing the game to Game Pass and continuing to support the FPS with big new updates. The latest of these, the Season 5 update, is out today, October 13.

Season 5 adds a new maps, including environments set in Las Vegas and Area 51, while it also brings something fans have been asking for since launch: a proper server browser. Check out the gameplay trailer above to see the Season 5 content in action.

Additionally, Battlefield Studios announced a Game of the Year Edition for Battlefield 6. The biggest selling point for the GOTY edition is the Ultimate Shortcut Kit, which instantly unlocks everything for all four classes, along with one season of Battlefield Pro, among other digital perks and extras.

The Ultimate Shortcut Kit, which was also available in other previous Battlefield games, is available to purchase by itself for $30.

title: God Of War’s Laufey Collector’s Edition Leaves One Important Thing Out: The Game
summary:
The God of War Laufey Collector's Edition has been revealed, but unlike the standard and digital deluxe editions that went up for preorder last month, this is purely a box of merch. The main attraction of this collector's edition is an eight-inch statue of Faye, Phranque the Cube, and Rue fighting against Begtse’s soldiers. Phranque will light up when connected to a USB power source.

The set also includes a deck of 51 illustrated oracle cards and a mini art book depicting the characters, creatures, and environments of God of War Laufey, all housed in collector's edition-packaging. As noted in the image, God of War Laufey is sold separately, and this edition costs $150. You'll need to shell out another $70 for a physical edition of the game to complete it. Preorders are now live on the PlayStation Direct Store ahead of the game's February 2027 release.

Sony has released several collector's editions in the past that bundled a digital download key for a game. A merchandise-only box set isn't uncommon, as just a few weeks ago, Rockstar Games revealed the $400 GTA 6 collector's edition that comes with plenty of stuff.

So what's the thinking behind one of these boxes? These boxes typically target dedicated, high-spending superfans who can afford to shell out extra for bonus physical content like this, acting as high-margin merchandise. At the same time, publishers can save some cash by not including the game, streamlining their supply chains and lowering production overhead in the process. Essentially, a bigger slice of the pie for companies, while consumers with deep pockets get limited-edition swag to display.

In other God of War news, the next game in the series will see Kratos return to the spotlight, and it'll pick up directly after the end of God of War Laufey. A live-action God of War TV series is also in development for Prime Video, and its new leading man, Dave Bautista, is already working to get shredded for the role after the original Kratos actor, Ryan Hurst, departed due to injury.

title: Best Witcher 3 Mods To Download For The Remaster
summary:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is considered one of the best RPGs of all time, but community members have still managed to design some incredible mods that alter, expand on, and improve it. Even after the Remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released, mod creators still managed to enhance the experience in one way or another.

Mods for The Witcher 3 range from quality-of-life changes, to redesigns of gameplay mechanics, to full-on DLC add-ons with new quests and content. While The Witcher 3 doesn’t have quite the expansive library of mods that Skyrim or Fallout 4 do on Nexus Mods, there are still dozens that make the game better in one way or another.

Below, you can see our picks for the 28 best mods to download for The Witcher 3. The mods are listed in no particular order, and all of these have been confirmed to be compatible with the Remastered version of the game. Also of note: cross-platform mod support for The Witcher 3 is fully functional in the Remastered version, but not every mod will necessarily be supported on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Better Call Ciri

  • Created by: pMarK
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Ciri sections in The Witcher 3 are some of the best parts of the entire game, as the young Witcher has so many unique abilities that Geralt simply doesn't have. Unfortunately, Ciri's sections are few and far between in the base game, but you can change that with the click of a button using the Better Call Siri mod.

This mod allows you to instantly change between Geralt and Ciri, regardless of where you are in The Witcher 3. You'll also have access to all of Ciri's abilities, and she can even fast travel and use Roach. However, you won't be able to earn XP as Ciri.

Advertisement

Monsters Reworked

  • Created by: Denroth
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The creatures of The Witcher 3 get their due in Monsters Reworked, an expansive mod that tackles all of the monsters in the game and its expansion. Denroth enhanced the visuals and modified more than textures to bring this project to fruition, and it’s truly an evolutionary step forward for the game.

In some cases, a complete or partial rework of the monsters was necessary to bring them up to a modern-gen standard. Those creatures have never looked better than they did after this. If anything, it makes battling the monsters even more fun, but be careful you don't get distracted admiring them while you’re trying to fight a battle. That’s just going to lead Geralt to a fatal end.

Advertisement

Tales of The Witcher

  • Created by: Gerwant
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

How’s this for ambition? Gerwant’s Tales of the Witcher jettisons the story of both the game and The Witcher novels, replacing them with a tale that takes place during Geralt’s first adventure in Cintra. It’s a brand-new story, with an emphasis on exploration and killing monsters. It feels like the expansion we never got, even though Tales of the Witcher remains a work in progress.

This mod was created with REDkit, and Gerwant has kept new updates coming since its release. For the final version, Gerwant is shooting for 25 hours of gameplay, 20 main quests, and a map that’s twice the size of The Witcher 3’s prologue playground map.

Advertisement

Custom Player Character

  • Created by: nikich340
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

This is one of the most intriguing Witcher 3 mods, because it gives players the chance to create their own characters and insert them into the game’s storyline. It not only offers fans the chance to set their character’s gender, it also has distinct male and female voices to choose from.

You could make your character a Witcher, but the more exciting aspect of this mod is that you can also choose to be a Sorceress. That entails a completely new combat system for magical attacks and a unique quest. Picking this option is like paving the way for a spin-off you never knew you wanted.

Advertisement

Firearms

  • Created by: Roenaxx
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Witcher 3 doesn’t have firearms, but this mod solves that problem by giving Geralt access to several weapons. Essentially, it allows Geralt to shoot his enemies in addition to all of his other attacks. Mod creator Roenaxx also added some thoughtful touches to keep this addition from unbalancing the game. The guns aren’t for sale, and players will have to complete a progression path to open them. Even if you do see that quest through to the end, bullets are going to be scarce.

If you want to stay well-armed in this world, then you’re gonna have to work for it by tracking down the materials you’ll need to craft bullets. You'll also need the Firearms compatibility mod to have it work with the Remastered version of The Witcher 3.

Advertisement

All Quest Objectives On Map

  • Created by: Wolfmark
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Witcher 3 is a game chock-full of quests you can take on. By default, you can only track one of these quests on the map at a time, which can get slightly tedious if you have multiple objectives in one location. If you download the All Quest Objectives On Map mod, though, you'll be able to track all of your quests at the same time and view them on the map, so you know exactly where to go for each of them.

Advertisement

Over 9000

  • Created by: GiecuMan
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

When you're out adventuring in the world, slaying monsters, and looting enemies, your inventory will get quite full, quite fast. You'll often find yourself dropping some valuable loot that you would have liked to carry, if only Geralt's pockets could handle it. To solve that issue, the Over 9000 mod makes it so you'll hopefully never exceed your carrying capacity again. The mod makes your carrying weight 9,000 pounds, which you'll likely never get near unless you're picking up every junk item you can find.

Advertisement

Fast Travel from Anywhere

  • Created by: JupiterTheGod
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

One of the more frustrating aspects of The Witcher 3 is being forced to make your way to signposts in order to fast travel to a destination. If you're not a fan of that mechanic, you can download the Fast Travel from Anywhere mod, which does exactly what the title says. No longer do you have to be at a signpost to fast travel; you can instead open your map and fast travel to any signpost you've previously visited on the map.

Advertisement

Sprint in Witcher Senses

  • Created by: MerseyRockoff
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

You might not realize it during your playthrough, but you spend quite a bit of time in Witcher Senses mode in The Witcher 3. The mechanic is used during dozens of quests, and it's required to progress in the game. However, Witcher Senses stops your ability to sprint, which can make the mechanic feel very sluggish to use.

To speed up your time while in the mode, though, all you have to do is download the Sprint in Witcher Senses mod. Now, you can move freely while using Witcher Senses and save quite a bit of time when tracking a beast or following a human's footsteps or blood trail.

Advertisement

Friendly HUD

  • Created by: wghost81
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The default heads-up display in The Witcher 3 is perfectly adequate, but if you're playing for a second or eighth time, you might want to change things up. The Friendly HUD mod makes a slew of changes to the vanilla HUD and even lets you customize what's shown on it. The mod also adds 3D quest and map markers, providing you with a more in-depth look at what an area holds. You're able to add and remove elements from the HUD while in-game using the mod's commands.

Advertisement

Switchable Cloaks

  • Created by: Priler
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

If you've read The Witcher books or watched the Netflix TV show, you know Geralt of Rivia is rarely seen without his famous cloak. In The Witcher 3, though, Geralt doesn't wear a cloak, instead opting for a set of brown armor by default. With the Geralt Cloak mod, you can fix that and make Geralt look like he does in the show and the books. The cloak is made of a dark fabric and covers Geralt's head, but it also comes with a cape. You can equip and take off both the cape and the hood through the mod's commands, as well as choose where and when the cloak and cape are shown.

Advertisement

The Gwent Card Dealer

  • Created by: Mangekyoumadara1987
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Gwent is one of the most popular aspects of The Witcher 3, and it has even inspired a full video game of its own that has become one of the best titles on Steam. However, trying to play Gwent properly in The Witcher 3 can be a slight hassle, as you have to collect more and more powerful cards as you progress. This becomes an issue, as Gwent cards are extremely hard to find. Of course, if you download The Gwent Card Dealer mod, you can bypass the grind of finding the cards yourself. This new merchant in The Witcher 3 sells 99% of cards, with some exceptions being those unique cards that you can only acquire in one specific way.

Advertisement

More Money For Traders

  • Created by: Tommy1984
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Traders in The Witcher 3 are an extremely useful resource, as they sell gear and items you need, as well as take unneeded loot off your hands for some quick cash. Unfortunately, the traders around the map often don't carry much money, leaving you to visit multiple traders to sell off all of your junk. With the More Money For Traders mod, though, that no longer becomes a problem. All traders on the map now restock their money supply every time you visit them, and have more cash to spend in general.

Advertisement

Slots Slots Slots

  • Created by: Krdemolition4
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

If you want to become truly overpowered in The Witcher 3, then you want as many skill sockets and mutation slots as possible. By default, you don’t have a ton of either, but the Slots Slots Slots mod changes that. The mod bumps the skill sockets from 12 and 16 to 18 and 26, while also adding four new mutation slots. You can now make Geralt a much tougher Witcher and utilize a more in-depth build.

Advertisement

Gallop Anywhere No Panic

  • Created by: alx713
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

When you arrive inside a major city in The Witcher 3, you immediately have some movement restrictions. Specifically, if you're riding Roach, you can only ride at a very slow pace through the city streets. Thanks to the Galloping In Cities mod, though, that restriction is fully lifted, allowing you to gallop through cities regardless of where you are, and making traveling to your destination a much quicker affair.

Advertisement

No Level Requirements

  • Created by: Dominitk666
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Every Witcher 3 player has experienced the sullen feeling of looting a new piece of gear and realizing they're not at the right level to equip it. You never have to experience that feeling again after downloading the No Level Requirements mod, as this makes it so every item and gear piece can be equipped regardless of your current level.

Advertisement

God Mode

  • Created by: jgheld and tnovak
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

God Mode is a mod that allows you to turn The Witcher 3 into whatever kind of game you want. The mod allows you to customize everything about your experience, turning the RPG into your personal playground. At the center of God Mode is the ability to become invincible, as you can reduce all enemy damage to zero so that Geralt never loses any HP. However, the mod can also give you unlimited money, items, carrying capacity, and a slew of other benefits that make The Witcher 3 easier. It's only recommended to download this mod if you're struggling with the game's mechanics and enemies, or if you've played through more than once.

Advertisement

Critical Slow Motion Combat Mod

  • Created by: KNGR, ksolberg, Halfmillz
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Combat in The Witcher 3 isn't everyone's cup of tea, and if you've been looking for a way to spice up your encounters with enemies, consider the Critical Slow Motion Combat mod. It adds a new slow motion element to combat, giving you the chance to outmaneuver enemies in a pinch and deal more damage in the process. There are new animations added with the mod, and you can choose when to activate the slow-mo while in combat.

Gwent Redux

  • Created by: oerdi25
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

Gwent is a mini-game that can stretch over hours in The Witcher 3. However, if you're looking to get even more out of the card game, you can download the Gwent Redux mod. It makes changes to the default cards, adds more than 100 new cards to your potential deck, improves opponent AI, and alters other parts of Gwent to make it more balanced and enjoyable. The mod changes quite a bit, so make sure you read its description to see everything that comes with downloading it.

Unlimited Roach Stamina

  • Created by: liongvn
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

We all love Roach as a character, but as a horse, he can be quite annoying at times. One of the more frustrating things about Roach is how quickly his stamina depletes, forcing you to slowly meander a path until the stamina recharges. Luckily, the Infinite Roach Stamina mod allows Roach to never stop galloping in The Witcher 3. With the mod installed, Roach never has to recharge his stamina bar, which is quite useful for the horse races on the map or in general travel.

Advertisement

Witcher 3 Quests Extended

  • Created by: PaulR0013
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The quests in The Witcher 3 are some of the deepest and most enjoyable you'll find in an RPG. However, after you've done them all multiple times, they can get a little stale. If you're searching for new quests to take on, grab the Witcher 3 Quests Extended mod. It adds 18 new quests to the game, some of which require either the Hearts of Stone or Blood and Wine expansions. However, there are plenty of quests that can be accessed in the base game, too. Check out the mod's description page to see how and where to start these quests.

Immersive Sounds

  • Created by: TheMenxceX
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Witcher 3's gameplay sounds are iconic. However, the Immersive Sounds mod takes the sounds you hear while exploring and in combat to another level. The mod makes all of the sounds clearer and punchier, adding some impact behind your in-game actions.

Yet Another Crossbow Rework

  • Created by: blibby84
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The crossbow isn't the strongest weapon in the default version of The Witcher 3. That thought process can be changed with the Crossbow Rework mod, though, which makes the crossbow much stronger in general by balancing all of its in-game stats. Witcher 2 Potion Length

  • Created by: mindkiller316
  • Download link: Nexus Mods

  • Download link: Nexus Mods

The Blood and Steel mod for The Witcher 3 changes up combat in several different ways. The most noticeable change the mod makes is to the dodging mechanic, which is now much faster and more reactive, allowing you to escape a sticky situation with more precision.   • Created by: mindkiller316
